problems: The blind guess (a martini-style cocktail glass with a long stem and garnish at lower right) does not match a kite. The closest alternative was the 7/1 single stroke, which fits the diagonal run better than the head-plus-tail layout.

The kite head is a thin sliver. The blue outline hugs the gold triangle (crown 93244 at about (299,108), left wingtip 95447 at about (127,193), foot 93867 at about (248,219)), so it reads as a copy of the gold lines, not a filled silhouette. There is no right wingtip, so the kite has no body.
Bridle knot 93747 at about (260,142) sits inside the sliver. Its label collides with the crown label, and the left wingtip label crosses the gold line.
The first tail knot 94477 at about (202,464) is roughly 245px below the foot, not just below it, so the tail reads as a detached stroke.
The tail is a long, wobbly blue loop, not a tapered streamer. Second knot 92946 at about (326,409) and end 91975 at about (404,470) are placed correctly.
Orientation is upright (kite at top, tail hanging down). Crown, left wingtip and foot are on the right parts.
output.advice: Redraw the kite as a filled silhouette, not a sliver around gold lines. Use a diamond roughly 90-120px wide, with crown 93244 at about (299,108) at the top and foot 93867 at about (248,219) at the bottom. Add the missing right wingtip so left wingtip 95447 at about (127,193) has a mirror partner on the right near (300,190). Place bridle knot 93747 as a small ring on the face at about (260,142), inside the diamond, with its label offset from the crown label. Move first tail knot 94477 up to about (240,240), just below the foot. Draw the tail as a tapered, slightly curved streamer from the foot through second knot 92946 at about (326,409) to the loose end 91975 at about (404,470), thick at the base and thin at the tip. Keep the figure upright and push labels clear of the strokes.
